correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all quantities from the symmetric geometric mass function. The first absolute moment gives the exact parameter cutoff. For \(B\le1\), every noncentral mass is increasing in the geometric parameter, so two admissible laws have exactly one sign change: the more concentrated law has excess mass only at zero. The Ky–Fan coupling representation then gives the exact Lévy–Prokhorov distance. The one-dimensional CDF formula gives the exact \(W_1\) distance, and their ratio simplifies to a function increasing in both parameters. Taking a coalescing pair at the moment boundary proves sharpness. The packaged verifier checks the formulas independently on a deterministic grid.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly isolates logarithm removal in the \(W_1\)-versus-Lévy--Prokhorov comparison as an open structural issue. The symmetric geometric family is a canonical discrete log-affine model and is named in the same paper. Determining the exact sharp linear constant, together with its complete moment-budget profile, shows that the logarithm is not forced by this natural heavy-tailed log-concave benchmark and supplies a quantitative target for any general improvement. The result is not an arbitrary parameter evaluation: it resolves the entire family under exactly the normalization used by the source.
